column4: The section treats creation as giving each thing a measured, fitting form; this ayah says that the Lord gave every thing its creation and then guided it, joining form to function.
Immediately after the creation and proportioning cited from 87:2, this ayah adds determining measure and guiding; it completes the section's claim that making something fit begins in measure.
After 82:7 names creating, proportioning, and balancing, this ayah says that God assembled the human being in whatever form He willed, adding construction from parts to the craft sequence.
After 78:12 builds seven strong structures above, this ayah places a blazing lamp there, making the constructed cosmic ceiling into a furnished and illuminated one.
The section furnishes a room in the Garden; Pharaoh's wife asks God here to build for her, near Him, a house in the Garden, directly joining divine building, room, and final abode.

The section makes room and landscape two scales of one craft; this ayah says Thamud made palaces on the plains and carved houses from the mountains, bringing ground, mountain, and dwelling into one construction scene.
The section moves between a prepared room and erected mountains; this ayah has Thamud carve secure houses out of the mountains themselves.
The room-world image meets at the mountain here: the people carve houses skillfully or proudly from mountains, applying deliberate workmanship to the section's great upright objects.

The section compares a leveled world-surface with a laid room-floor; this ayah presents a palace paved smooth with glass that is mistaken for natural water, deliberately blurring constructed interior and landscape.
The section lists four objects marked by the work performed on them; this ayah likewise lists chambers, statues, basin-like dishes, and fixed cauldrons as things craftsmen make for Solomon.
Before the sky is raised and the balance placed in 55:7, this ayah says the sun and moon run by calculation, giving cosmic motion the same exact order the section finds in cosmic construction.
The section reads the sky as a prepared ceiling; this ayah places constellations in the sky and sets within it a lamp and illuminating moon, furnishing that ceiling with lights.
Within the construction sequence of 79:27-32, this ayah brings water and pasture out of the spread earth, showing the leveled floor made habitable rather than merely shaped.
After sky, earth, water, pasture, and mountains are prepared in 79:27-32, this ayah calls them provision for people and their livestock, reconnecting the built world to the section's camel.
The section raises roofs and arranges a habitable room; this ayah confronts a town fallen in upon its roofs, then uses its revival as a sign of resurrection.
The section grounds skilled making in straightness and sound measure; this ayah contrasts a building founded on reverence with one built on a crumbling edge that collapses with its builder into fire.
The section presents the current earth and sky as a completed room; this ayah marks the Day when earth is exchanged for another earth and the heavens also, setting a boundary on that construction.
The section's roof is raised over an inhabited floor; this ayah evokes destroyed settlements whose buildings have collapsed upon their roofs, reversing the stable room-form.
Against the section's purposeful measured construction, this ayah rebukes building a monument on every height merely in play, distinguishing skilled form from purposeless display.
Continuing 26:128's rebuke, this ayah faults the making of massive structures as though their builders would live forever, exposing the false permanence of worldly construction.

The section imagines the maker's hand arranging and raising a dwelling; this ayah has people ruin their own houses with their hands and the believers' hands, turning the handwork of habitation into dismantling.
The section extends measured creation from world to human form; this ayah says God shapes people in the wombs however He wills, a hidden instance of the same fitting craft.
The section bases the world's made order on measure; this ayah makes night a repose and the sun and moon a means of calculation, giving the inhabited cosmos temporal measure.
The section finds exact proportion beneath creation; this ayah determines measured stations for the moon so people can know years and reckoning, an ordered celestial counterpart.
In the context of what wombs bear, diminish, and increase, this ayah says every thing with God is according to a measure, extending the section's craft-measure into hidden growth.
The section treats the made world as both measured and furnished; this ayah says that nothing is sent from God's treasuries except in a known measure, connecting provision to exact apportionment.
The section joins creature, mountain, tent, and house; this ayah directs the bee to take houses in mountains, trees, and human trellises, another meeting of habitation with the made landscape.
The section links upright construction to straightness; this ayah has the barrier raised between mountain sides until the iron mass is made level with them, then finished with molten copper.
The prose defines صف as arranging things on one straight line; this ayah tells Pharaoh's magicians to assemble their scheme and then come in a single row.
The section's constructed cosmos rests on ordered measure; this ayah creates night, day, sun, and moon and gives each its own swimming course.
The section presents creation as a sequence of fitted acts; this ayah narrates successive transformations from drop through bones and flesh to another creation, then praises the best of creators.
The prose explains بث as spreading created beings through earth; with a different verb, this ayah says God multiplied or dispersed people in earth and will gather them back to Him.
The section's Garden interior is high and prepared for its inhabitants; this ayah rewards the patient with the lofty chamber and a greeting of peace.
The section furnishes the Garden as a dwelling; this ayah promises believers chambers in the Garden with rivers below, where they remain.
The prose pairs creation with living beings spread on earth; this ayah says God created humans from dust and then they became people dispersing across the earth.
Following 32:7-8's account of excellent creation, this ayah says God proportioned the human being and breathed into him, supplying the finishing act of that craft.
The section's raised room belongs to final security; this ayah says those brought near are secure in the Garden's chambers.
The section grounds cosmic making in exact measure; this ayah describes the sun running to an appointed point and calls that the determination of the Mighty, Knowing.
Alongside the sun's determination in 36:38, this ayah says God measured stages for the moon, another explicit act of fitting the sky's contents to order.
This ayah distinguishes the courses of sun, moon, night, and day and gives each an orbit, spelling out the non-overlap produced by the measurement in 36:38-39.
Before 41:12 orders the sky into seven heavens and adorns the nearest one, this ayah addresses the smoke-like sky and earth and records their willing submission to being formed.
Immediately before the vessels and cups of 43:71, this ayah admits the faithful and their spouses into the Garden rejoicing, identifying the inhabitants for whom that hospitality is arranged.
Immediately after the raised beds of 56:34, this ayah says the Garden companions were brought forth in a special creation, meeting the furnished room with a new act of making.
The section unfolds creation through measuring, shaping, and setting in order; this ayah gathers the divine names Creator, Originator, and Former, distinguishing those aspects of making.
The section says that making begins with due measure; in a promise about trust and provision, this ayah says God has appointed a measure for every thing.
The prose hears living beings broadcast across the prepared earth; using a different verb, this ayah says God spread humankind throughout earth and will gather them to Him.
After 71:15's layered heavens, this ayah places the moon within them as light and the sun as a lamp, adding illumination to the section's roof-like sky.
The section moves from placing objects in a room to measured creation; this ayah places the human drop in a firm lodging, the womb, within the measuring sequence completed in 77:23.
After the drop is lodged for a known term, this ayah says that God measured and is the excellent measurer, directly restating the craft principle developed in the section.
